title: Deepfake detection research
lines: July to November 2026
Vaibhav Shiroorkar | Shivansh Gupta | Adithya Jithesh
Equal credit: one third each
Guide: Dr. Tejashree Phatak
notes: Introduce the research question: whether different detection cues help on unfamiliar media. Explain that this talk covers two research lines with separate protocols.

title: Research question
lines: Do visual, speech and alignment cues transfer to unfamiliar media?
In-domain accuracy does not establish generalization.
Ranking, threshold errors and coverage answer different questions.
notes: Give the example of a real video with fake audio. The video label is genuine for a visual branch, but the clip-level label is fake. Comparisons must use the same target.

title: Two research lines
lines: Root: trained cue-specific branches and fusion.
Team: frozen encoders and separate module findings.
Separate splits, environments and experiment records.
Scores from the two protocols are not interchangeable.
notes: Both research lines receive equal team credit. Distinguish a shared research question from a shared evaluation. The team platform does not expose one validated fused verdict.

title: July to September
lines: July: five-stream design and first data pipeline.
August: trainers, encoder changes and evaluation rebuild.
September: branches, fusion and shortcut checks.
Historical scores must be read with later corrections.
notes: Describe the progression from working code to evidence that could be checked. Emphasize source-disjoint splits, preprocessing hashes and seed tracking. Do not revive withdrawn scores.

title: Evaluation controls
lines: Separate sources before fitting or selecting models.
Choose thresholds on validation data.
Freeze models before sealed evaluation.
Use group intervals and correct multiple comparisons.
notes: Explain why frames from one source cannot be treated as independent evidence. Hand over to Shivansh after four minutes total.

title: System architecture
lines: Root: preprocess -> cue-specific branches -> late fusion.
Team: preprocess -> frozen encoders -> task heads.
The platform reports findings for each available module.
Unavailable evidence can produce an inconclusive finding.
notes: Explain one input's path. The root fusion results have protocol defects discussed later. Experimental image and generated-video outputs must retain their limitations.

title: Team sealed results
lines: Video, Celeb-DF family: AUROC 0.6238 to 0.8218.
Speech, In-the-Wild: AUROC 0.7516 to 0.9148.
Against Xception: difference +0.0176.
Corrected interval [-0.0011, +0.0355] includes zero.
notes: These are MVP-to-final comparisons under the team protocol. The corrected interval is 98.33 percent. Claim non-inferiority at margin 0.0100, not corrected superiority. Xception used 224-pixel inputs.

title: Threshold errors matter
lines: A high AUROC can coexist with harmful threshold errors.
Face-video false positives: 0.1098 on Celeb-DF family.
Face-video false positives: 0.1405 on DFD.
These are post hoc rates at frozen thresholds.
notes: Define false-positive rate as the share of genuine videos called manipulated. These are seed-mean rates. They were computed after the freeze and are not confirmatory endpoints.

title: Root results needing reruns
lines: Outer-fold labels selected fusion branch checkpoints.
Zero-start LAV-DF windows could overlap manipulation.
PE and CLIP features used incorrect normalization.
Corrected performance remains unknown.
notes: Do not use the historical 0.9969 LAV-DF score or the 0.7527 PE score as corrected results. Explain nested cross-fitting and why a code fix is not a new measurement.

title: Post-freeze evaluations
lines: E-033 LAV-DF: 18,383 previously unread clips.
Any-modality label: video AUROC 0.2954; speech 0.6448.
E-034 image AUROC: 0.7909 on 7,209 images.
Exploratory evaluations on seen distributions.
notes: The report includes intervals. The E-033 target here is any modality changed, not the modality-specific G4 target. These are not new confirmatory tests. Hand over to Adithya after four minutes total.

title: What the diagnostics support
lines: E-034 PNG-only AUROC: 0.5693 on 368 images.
The smaller diagnostic population also changes content.
This is an association, not proof of a format cause.
Attention at chance does not prove timing is ignored.
notes: Describe the difference between a diagnostic and a causal intervention. For alignment, shifting or swapping audio would give stronger mechanism evidence. Nested sample groups are not independent replications.

title: November experiments
lines: AV-HuBERT support and mouth crops implemented.
E-035: preregistered zero-shot alignment baseline.
E-036: preregistered real-only and supervised heads.
Both result slots are empty. No improvement is claimed.
notes: Explain that implementation, preregistration and results are different stages. Preserve sealed-source exclusions. Root corrected reruns are a separate workstream.

title: Demonstration and reproduction
lines: Confirm local data, weights and the correct environment.
Explain each module's output and missing evidence.
Keep fixture or mock mode visibly labelled.
Trace research numbers to experiment IDs and hashes.
notes: Use the demonstration only if the required artifacts are available. Otherwise explain the documented workflow without claiming live inference. Do not rerun a sealed test for the talk.

title: Research conclusion
lines: Evaluation controls exposed failures hidden by accuracy.
The team sealed protocol measured specific improvements.
Root fusion and encoder claims still require reruns.
Deployment readiness and state-of-the-art performance are not established.
notes: The contribution is the documented testing and correction process. Avoid claiming novelty over all prior literature. The full research report lists evidence and limitations.

title: Equal credit and discussion
lines: Vaibhav Shiroorkar: one third.
Shivansh Gupta: one third.
Adithya Jithesh: one third.
Equal credit across all project work and deliverables.
notes: Author order does not imply rank. Each member presents five slides in four minutes and prepares the whole project. Acknowledge Dr. Tejashree Phatak separately as guide. Invite questions.
